title: Annotatio I §.IV: Synecdoche Grammar vs Rhetoric; Mansfeld’s Calvinian vs Lutheran metonymy
pass_a_gloss: From the latter, as to Synecdoche, besides Selneccer and Luther himself, innumerable others — yet with a distinction between Grammatical and Rhetorical Synecdoche, by whose application to the present matter how much is sinned against Grammar even those know who are not yet washed with bronze. For where, I ask, is Synecdoche handed down in the Grammars for such as these Theologians contend? Although Synecdoche, whether called Grammatical or coming under another name, remains nonetheless a trope and figure, just as metonymy, metaphor, or irony: Which the nature of a trope teaches, not to be removed or changed by dissimulation of the name when the thing itself is obtained. But as to Metonymy, Mansfeld in Erotemata on the four Visitatorial articles, about to grant metonymy no less in the definitive proposition of the prior part of the Sacred Supper than of the posterior This cup is the N.T. in my blood — yet under a distinction ridiculous enough between Calvinian Metonymy of sign and thing signified, and Lutheran Metonymy by which as effect is put for cause in this proposition The Cup is the Testament in my blood, i.e. the blood in the cup is that by which the N.T. is ratified, that is the promise of remission of sins; so Containing for contained in this: This bread is my Body.
pass_b_english: On synecdoche, Selneccer, Luther, and countless others distinguish Grammatical from Rhetorical synecdoche — a distinction that sins against Grammar for anyone not still wet behind the ears.
Call it Grammatical or not: synecdoche remains a trope, like metonymy, metaphor, or irony.

Mansfeld grants metonymy in both halves of the Institution, yet under a rather ridiculous split between Calvinian sign/thing-signified metonymy and Lutheran effect-for-cause / container-for-content metonymy.
source_text: Ex posterioribus, quà Synechdochen, praeter Selneccerum ipsumque Lutherum, innumeri alii, cum distinctione tamen inter Synechdochen Grammaticam & Rhetoricam, cujus Distinctionis applicatione ad praesentem materiam, quantum in Grammaticam peccetur, vel illi norunt, qui nondum aere lavantur. Nam ubi quaeso traditur in Grammaticis Synecdoche, pro quali contendunt Theologi hi? Quanquam Synecdoche, sive Grammatica dicatur, sive alio veniat nomine, tropus tamen ac figura remanet, juxta ac metonymia, metaphora aut ironia: Id quod docet tropi natura, nominis dissimulatione haud tollenda nec mutanda, cùm ipsa re obtinetur. Quà Metonymiam autem, Mansrafius in Erotematibus ad articulos quatuor Visitatorios, non minus in propositione definitiva partis prioris Sacrae Coenae, quàm posterioris ista: Hoc poculum, est N. T. in sanguine meo, metonymiam largiturus, sed sub distinctione satis ridicula inter Metonymiam Calvinianam de signo & signato, & Metonymiam Lutheranam, quâ uti effectus pro causa ponitur, in hac propositione: Poculum est Testamentum in sanguine meo, i. e. sanguis in poculo est illud quo sancitum est N. T., id est promissio remissionis peccatorum; ita Continens pro contento in hac: Hic panis est Corpus meum.
